ns2:section.sectionText: This course introduces students to the practical craft of program evaluation, particularly to the practices that distinctively characterize evaluation in the field. These practices include determining which evaluation approach to use in a given context; negotiating evaluation contracts or agreements with clients; figuring out one’s role as evaluator, as well as one’s relationship with stakeholders; understanding the political dynamics of an evaluation context and situating the evaluation therein; and establishing ongoing communication and reporting processes. The class will work collaboratively on one or more evaluation designs of local and practical initiatives on or near campus that allow students opportunity to work in diverse settings to apply basic tools and methods of social science to program evaluation contexts, such as data collection tools, qualitative and quantitative analysis, and reporting of design results. The course is best taken after an introduction to evaluation theory or after at least one course in social science inquiry methods. The work requires some basic skills in social science methods. Ideally, students would have taken either EPSY 470, 480 and/or with approval of instructor.
